newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Venice holds conference to promote quality beef.
newsitem.headline: Venice holds conference to promote quality beef.

text.p: The first scientific congress to review measures taken by the European Union to restore consumer confidence in beef after the mad cow crisis is to be held in Venice in April, the organisers announced on Thursday.

European Quality Beef (EQB), an umbrella organisation formed by producers, processors and distributors from 10 European Union countries, say that the two-day conference on April 11/12 will be a launch for a European quality beef promotion campaign.
"The congress will be the first major event to promote beef as a quality product in which people can have absolute confidence," Claude Herbaut the French campaign co-ordinator told a news conference.

It is the first time that a promotional campaign has been funded by the EU which is paying 50 percent of the 64-million- ecu budget to restore consumer confidence damaged by Bovine Spongiform Encephalopthy (BSE), Herbaut added.
"We have had problems because of mad cow disease and the congress will focus on legislation, health and veterinary issues as well as the importance of beef in a balanced diet," he added.
EU support for the quality beef campaign is a result of the mad cow crisis blamed for depressing beef sales in the EU and for undermining consumer confidence.

Beef carrying the campaign's new blue and green logo is guaranteed to conform with strict rules covering production, transport and slaughter as well as ensuring that animals and meat products can be traced back to their origins.
Senior Commission agriculture official Fabio Gencarelli said that the new European quality beef logo currently applied to 200,000 tonnes of beef produced in the European Union.
"We hope that the figure will reach 500,000 tonnes which represents 10 percent of European beef production. I see no reason why it shouldn't," he told the news conference.
